| [LIT-037](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-037.md) v3 | The Open Systems View | Cuffaro & Hartmann (2021), [ARXIV-2112.11095](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.11095). The paper argues philosophically, not formally, that the quantum theory of open systems "GT" is more fundamental than standard closed-system quantum theory "ST". GT treats states as density operators that evolve, in general, non-unitarily, and it admits not-completely-positive maps. The ontic and epistemic cases each win only on a second, interpretation- or practice-laden criterion: OntFund-2 and EpFund-2. On the first, formal criteria (OntFund-1, EpFund-1) the two frameworks tie, and the authors say so because Stinespring dilation and dropping the Lindblad terms translate in both directions (§4.1, §4.2.1). Explanatory fundamentality is granted only deflationarily (ExFund-1), and the authors recommend dropping the notion (§4.2.2). The step from there to "the open systems view is fundamental tout court" (§4.3) rests on the special sciences and on "there are no other options". | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 (NOTE-077); worth reading as the clearest statement of the "open systems view" and of the distinction between a view, a framework, a theory and a model (§2, §4.1, §5.2). The ontic form is motivated by quantum non-individuality and entanglement, gauge symmetry and the hole argument. | [LIT-062](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-062.md) v3 | On the reality of the quantum state | Pusey et al. (2011), [ARXIV-1111.3328](https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.3328). Take pure states \|ψ0⟩, \|ψ1⟩ with \|⟨ψ0\|ψ1⟩\| = cos θ. Assume (a) a model assigns each preparation a distribution µ_i(λ) over physical states, (b) n independent preparations yield the product distribution µ_{x1}(λ1)⋯µ_{xn}(λn), and (c) outcome probabilities depend only on (λ1, …, λn). If the model's predictions are within ε of quantum theory, then D(µ0, µ1) ≥ 1 − 2ε^{1/n} for any n with 2^{1/n} − 1 ≤ tan(θ/2) (Eq. 7, App. B). At ε = 0 the distributions for distinct pure states cannot overlap on a set of non-zero measure, so Harrigan–Spekkens ψ-epistemic models are ruled out. | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 (NOTE-030); the founding ψ-ontology theorem. It is short, fully proved (App. A–B), and still the reference that every later ψ-epistemic/ψ-ontic argument, including LIT-007 §I.C and LIT-090, positions itself against. | [LIT-096](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-096.md) | What Is It Like to Be a Bat? | Nagel (1974), [DOI-10.2307/2183914](https://doi.org/10.2307/2183914). An organism has conscious states if and only if there is something it is like to be that organism. That subjective character belongs to a type of point of view, and it is left out by every functional, intentional or causal analysis, since each is compatible with its absence. Reduction elsewhere moves away from a point of view toward the objective; here that move leads away from the thing being explained. So physicalism may be true, but we have no conception of how it could be. Nagel proposes an "objective phenomenology" that would describe experience to beings who cannot have it. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 (NOTE-089); the source of the "something it is like" criterion of consciousness that the record's AI-consciousness work (LIT-056) adopts as its target, and of the argument that no functional analysis can settle whether that criterion is met. |

| [LIT-122](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-122.md) v2 | The Representation of Time and Change in Mechanics | Belot (2005), DOI-10.1016/B978-044451560-5/50005-1. For theories with ideal existence, uniqueness and a dynamical time-translation group, time is three intertwined ℝ-actions (on spacetime, on the symplectic space of solutions, and on the isomorphic space of initial data), and change is a slicing-indexed family of functions on those spaces. Singular dynamics, gauge freedom and time-dependence each damage this picture in a repairable way. Spatially compact vacuum GR breaks it, because the reduced Hamiltonian vanishes (h ≡ 0) and there is only one canonical isomorphism between the reduced spaces. That is the problem of time. It is not an artefact of the 3+1 split, it does not show change to be illusory, and it is absent from asymptotically flat GR and from artificially generally covariant theories. A parameterized "geometric time", such as CMC, restores change and, in the CMC case, a time-dependent Hamiltonian flow. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-118](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-118.md)); worth reading as the careful technical-philosophical statement of what the problem of time is and is not in classical GR. The paper defines the individualized (ecological) niche as the environmental conditions under which a particular individual has an expected lifetime reproductive success of ≥ 1, counting each offspring as 0.5 per parent in outcrossers. The authors split it into five sub-concepts: realized (A), potential (B), time-slice (C), prospective (D) and trajectory-based (E), plus a "fundamental individualized niche" set aside as practically interchangeable with the potential niche. The individual niche has n + s dimensions, adding intraspecific axes such as density and morph frequency. Its boundary is the expected-LRS isocline of 1, which is estimable only by marginalizing fitness functions across individuals. The authors themselves call the concept "mostly of a metaphorical value". | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-170](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-170.md)); worth reading as the clearest structuring of the "individualized niche" vocabulary, and as the individual-level complement to Trappes ([LIT-169](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-169.md)); it is a behavioural-ecology position essay, and its own admission that the potential niche is unobservable and estimable only from population-level marginalization limits it to a framework rather than a measurement result. |
| [LIT-131](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-131.md) v2 | A Model of Understanding in Deep Learning Systems | Freeborn (2026), [ARXIV-2604.04171](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.04171). The Fractured Understanding Hypothesis (§7.5), which the paper argues for but does not test, says the understanding deep networks reach is characteristically symbolically misaligned, non-reductive, locally fractured, proxy-dependent and representationally fragmented. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 (NOTE-123); worth reading as a careful, explicitly "thin" explication that turns the proxy disputes (memorization vs generalization, interpolation vs extrapolation) into testable conditions. Across three Prolific studies (N = 198, 673, 142; Likert 1–7), judgments that "X happened because the agent wanted X" track intentionality judgments under manipulations of luck. Across the 12 condition means, r = .98. Causation only partly mediates the effect of luck (64%, 45% and 49%; exploratory analyses). As the causal account predicted, Study 3 found that the effect of Process (normal vs mix-up) on intentionality is larger when the agent knows how the buttons work (interaction F(1, 423) = 32). In the morally neutral Kraemer vignette, intentionality and causation came apart. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-092](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-092.md)); Worth reading as the cleanest current statement and test of the causal (desire-causes-outcome) account of folk intentionality under luck. | [LIT-135](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-135.md) v3 | Conscious artificial intelligence and biological naturalism | Seth (2024), DOI-10.1017/S0140525X25000032. Seth argues that conscious AI needs computational functionalism *and* substrate flexibility extending to silicon, and that both are doubtful (§3.9). Against them he gives a positive, explicitly non-vitalist case, running from interoceptive predictive processing through the free energy principle to autopoiesis, that consciousness is a property "of only (but not necessarily all) living systems" (§4). He concludes that real artificial consciousness is "unlikely along current trajectories" and would need "living AI" (§5.8), while conscious-*seeming* AI is "almost certain" and may be "cognitively impenetrable" (§6.2). He concedes that "my case is not watertight" (§5.8). | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-169](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-169.md)); worth reading as the leading statement of biological naturalism about AI, with a useful five-scenario map (Table 1) of what conscious AI would require. | [LIT-139](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-139.md) v2 | Inductive Risk and Values in Science | Douglas (2000), DOI-10.1086/392855. Hempel's "inductive risk" (the chance of wrongly accepting or rejecting a hypothesis) arises at three internal stages of science: choosing a methodology such as a significance level, characterising data, and interpreting results. Wherever the non-epistemic consequences of error can be foreseen, weighing them requires non-epistemic values. Douglas shows this on dioxin cancer studies. Three pathologist panels (1978, 1980, 1990) scored the same Kociba rat-liver slides differently (e.g. 34/50, 33/47, 18/50 tumours at 100 ng/kg/day). Choosing between threshold and no-threshold readings of the same data has meant regulatory limits about 100× apart. Values enter only indirectly, through the consequences of error, never as evidence that a claim is true. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-145](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-145.md)); worth reading as the canonical, compact statement of the modern inductive-risk argument. | [LIT-140](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-140.md) v2 | Large Language Models Are Stochastic Measuring Devices | Mallory (2025), DOI-10.1093/9780191998317.003.0003. The chapter argues by analogy that deep neural networks are "stochastic measuring devices". Training alters the parameters in response to data, so that the resulting configuration carries information about the data ("training is measurement"). The trained weights are a model, and generation is simulation. DNNs are stochastic because random initialisation and non-convex loss mean runs need not converge to the same weights, failing Baird's "regularity" condition. The problems of interpreting model states and generated text are therefore the familiar problems of instruments, models and simulations. The problem of interpretable AI is an instance of the coordination problem in the philosophy of measurement. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-090](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-090.md)); worth reading as the most developed instrument-centred alternative to agentive framings of LLMs, and for its tidy division into model-interpretation, text-interpretation and linking problems; it offers an analogy, not a refutation (its own words, § Interpretation and Communication), and should be read in the published OUP version where possible. |
| [LIT-141](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-141.md) v3 | Emergence: from physics to biology, sociology, and computer science | McKenzie (2025), [ARXIV-2508.08548](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.08548). Sole-authored survey by a condensed-matter physicist. It takes novelty (a property the parts lack) as the defining mark of emergence and sets it against twelve other characteristics in §2. The six "objective" ones are discontinuities, order, modification of parts, universality, diversity and mesoscale modularity. The six "subjective" ones are self-organisation, unpredictability, irreducibility, contextuality/downward causation, complexity and intra-stratum closure. Case studies from the Ising model to Schelling segregation and LLMs show that each can come apart from novelty: novelty without discontinuity (Kondo, Fermi liquids, spin ice), without unpredictability (BKT, spin ice), and with reduction (Butterfield). §22 sides with weak emergence and argues that strong-emergence claims from molecular structure are weak. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 (NOTE-124); worth reading as a hub reference and example catalogue on emergence from physics outward, with unusually concrete case studies and a sceptical physicist's §15 on molecular structure. | [LIT-143](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-143.md) v2 | What is a Mathematical Structure of Conscious Experience? | Kleiner & Ludwig (2023), [ARXIV-2301.11812](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.11812). The paper proposes a definition, (MSC). A mathematical structure S = ((A_i), (S_j)) is a structure *of* conscious experience iff (S1) its domains are sets of experiential aspects, and (S2) every relation or function S_j has an "S_j-aspect". An S_j-aspect is an aspect that a variation of experience changes exactly when the variation fails to preserve S_j. The older condition (MDC), that a structure is "of" experience if its domains are aspects and its axioms hold, survives only as the necessary condition for *describing* experience, because as a sufficient condition it admits incompatible structures (discrete and non-discrete topologies on the same set), arbitrary re-definitions (every C·d for C > 0) and consciousness-indifferent structures. Worked examples: experienced relative similarity is a strict partial order that satisfies (MSC), given transitivity (assumed). Visual regions form a topology that satisfies (MSC), given Bayne and Chalmers's subsumptive unity thesis. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 (NOTE-135); worth reading as the most explicit criterion for when a formal model is *of* experience rather than a convenient description of it. Its two positive results are conditional: transitivity of relative similarity is assumed, and the topology result assumes the subsumptive unity thesis. Cite the Synthese version, which has dropped v1's argument against metric structure. |

A position paper, not an argument to a conclusion. | [LIT-150](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-150.md) v3 | What is emergence, after all? | Rizi (2025), [ARXIV-2507.04951](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.04951). A perspective, not an argument with results. He says the onset of emergence is located by order parameters, diverging susceptibility and correlation length, and RG fixed points, and that dualities show macro behaviour is not dictated by micro "stuff". Wallace argues that reading a physical theory "math-first", as mathematical models plus representation rather than as sentences aiming at truth, already makes scientific realism structural. Math-first theoretical equivalence and reduction (as instantiation) are coarse-grained enough to dissolve the standard underdetermination and theory-change objections. On this footing epistemic and ontic structural realism differ only in whether metaphysics itself is language-first or math-first. On math-first OSR, objects are whatever the best "predicate precisification" of a theory quantifies over, real patterns are defined through instantiation plus best precisification, and ontology is scale-relative. (2) The relata-need-relations regress is blocked by Eddington's "package hypothesis": not all relata are logically prior to relations. Hazelwood defines RC as "the process of natural selection is both a cause and effect of processes such as niche construction" and EC as "natural selection is an emergent causal process". He argues they are incompatible. Emergence here is Wilson's synchronic dependence plus autonomy, cashed out as Pence's composition. If EC holds, niche construction partly composes selection, so the two fail Woodward's independent-fixability condition and cannot stand in a causal relation. | [LIT-157](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-157.md) v3 | Reproducees, reproducers, and Darwinian individuals | Bourrat (2025), DOI-10.1007/s11229-024-04880-w. Bourrat builds a nested vocabulary. A reproducee is a B that comes after A, is caused by A, and is of A's relevant class. A reproducer is a reproducee with reproductive autonomy, meaning it can reproduce across a range of backgrounds. A Darwinian individual is a reproducer with high reproductive causal control, meaning heredity survives as the parent's description is made finer. On that vocabulary, genes of multicellular organisms are, like hearts, mere reproducees, but with high control. Material overlap is necessary for reproducers, which are whole life cycles, and unnecessary for reproducees, so Griesemer and Godfrey-Smith partly talk past each other. Lloyd's own four-question anatomy of "unit of selection": interactor, reproducer (formerly replicator), manifestor of adaptation, and beneficiary. Every experiment and every replication rests on individuation judgments about what is being manipulated and measured ("conceptual scope"). So direct replication can at most help rule out random error, and "perhaps" establish that some effect exists but not which effect, while conceptual replication begs the question by presupposing that two operationalisations individuate the same effect. | [LIT-164](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-164.md) v3 | Wave-Function Realism and the Scope of Physical Causal Closure | Poltorak (2026), <https://philsci-archive.pitt.edu/30720/>. A closure principle has two tacit parameters, its domain and its completeness relation (causal, dynamical or explanatory). Wave-function realism falsifies spatiotemporal-domain closure (STC) but is compatible with fundamental-physical closure (FPC), so there is no "trans-domain causal breach". The physicalist is left with a dilemma: STC is too narrow, and FPC needs an independent criterion of physicality plus a dynamical-to-causal bridge. Trappes compares NCT's evolutionary niche with the ecological niche. The evolutionary niche is the sum of selection pressures on a population (Odling-Smee, Laland & Feldman 2003), read "externally" as the environmental factors that produce fitness differences. On that reading spontaneous symmetry breaking preserves the symmetry across the degenerate vacua, and the DHR analysis derives quantum statistics from the algebra. What OSR gets right about symmetry, entanglement and particle kinds is better captured by "metaphysical coherentism": object-like entities (in one domain) stand in symmetric *partial* ontological dependence on one another. Worrall argues that the EBM evidence hierarchy has no sound general rationale for giving randomisation extra epistemic weight, even though it lets high-quality RCTs "trump any number of observational studies". He examines five standard arguments. Four fail: (a) Fisher's significance-test logic, (b) control of unknown confounders, (d) that observational studies "exaggerate" effects, and (e) probabilistic causality. The fifth, (c) selection bias, is a "cast-iron argument", but it supports only taking allocation out of the clinicians' hands, and randomisation is one way to do that. What matters is balance on plausible confounders, a placebo or active control and blinding. Its one technical rule is that an amplitude W(b,a) gives the probability P = \|W\|² only when a and b are relative to the same system. That rule removes the clash between P_collapse = Σᵢ\|W(c,bᵢ)\|²\|W(bᵢ,a)\|² and P_unitary = \|ΣᵢW(c,bᵢ)W(bᵢ,a)\|² (eqs. 2–4). The paper sets out an idealized three-stage sequence of interaction types, which it calls a "first and rough sketch" (§1). Stage 1 is coordination in *collections* (pairwise, "aggregative" interactions of co-located individuals). Stage 2 is cooperation in *conexuses* (a connected web of binary interactions whose benefits can still be counted per member). Stage 3 is collaboration in *communities*: heterogeneous multi-way interactions around a shared goal, in which generatively entrenched "core" interactions give organizational closure. The paper asserts, rather than argues, that this describes evolutionary transitions non-circularly and that individuality is a special case of collectivity. The paper argues that "naturalizing teleology" serves at least two relatively autonomous projects with different success criteria. The philosophical argument is thin in places, notably the Gödel-based case that it is "not a tautology", so it should be read as one side of the dispute and not as a settlement of it. |
| [LIT-210](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-210.md) v2 | Philosophy of Microbiology | O'Malley & Parke (2020), <https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/microbiology/>. O'Malley & Parke argue in four steps that philosophy should attend to microbes. Microbes do most of the planet's biological work and underlie every major transition. Microbiology founded medicine, molecular biology and genomics. Microbes are unusually good material models, including for phenomena once defined by animals (predation, ageing, kin recognition, cognition). Microbiome research bears on individuality and causation. They are sceptical about the strongest microbiome claims. Whether host and microbiome form one unit of selection is "still disputed". Claims that microbiomes change the "self" are "usually expressed in very vague language". The 2026 revision adds that Asgard-archaea phylogenies may make eukaryogenesis "first and foremost a story about diversification within Archaea" rather than a transition in individuality. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-159](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-159.md)); worth reading as a short, current (April 2026) orientation to where microbes change philosophy of biology, with a useful deflationary check on microbiome-and-self claims. It is a survey with no thesis beyond "pay attention to microbes"; for individuality it points onward to the Biological Individuals ([LIT-168](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-168.md)) and Units and Levels of Selection ([LIT-160](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-160.md)) entries. |
| [LIT-211](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-211.md) v3 | What Lives? A meta-analysis of diverse opinions on the definition of life | Bender et al. (2025), [ARXIV-2505.15849](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.15849). Three LLMs (Claude 3.7 Sonnet, GPT-4o, Llama 3.3 70B), each run 3 times on both orderings of every pair, rated 68 hand-solicited definitions of life on a −1 to 1 "correlation" rubric. The averaged matrix, cut by complete-linkage clustering at an elbow, gives 8 clusters, 45/68 of them (66%) in "Cognitive Autonomy" (n=24) and "Dissipative Self-Organizing Systems" (n=21). The clusters are weak: the repo's own saved statistics give an overall silhouette of 0.079, and cross-model agreement is an unadjusted Rand index of 71–79% against a chance level of about 62–74%. The headline that life is "a continuous semantic landscape" is not tested against any alternative. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 (NOTE-109); worth reading as a dataset: 68 signed, three-sentence definitions of life from named researchers, with a manual thematic coding (Table 1). Its computational conclusions are weakly supported and are better read as illustrations than as findings. |
| [LIT-213](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-213.md) v2 | Rigour versus the need for evidential diversity | Cartwright (2021), DOI-10.1007/s11229-021-03368-1. Cartwright offers a characterisation of "rigour": a method is rigorous when a valid argument shows its results are evidence for the conclusion and its premises are well established or secured by design. On that definition even well-run RCTs often fail to rigorously establish a study-population ATE, because orthogonality holds only at assignment and the potential-outcomes premise carries heavy metaphysics, and they seldom answer singular questions. Her alternative is a causal-process-tracing theory of change (pToC) with five elements (steps, causal principles, support factors, derailers, safeguards). It catalogues the diverse and mostly non-rigorous evidence that singular causal predictions need. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-161](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-161.md)); worth reading as a compact, citable statement of the "rigour is overvalued, evidence the causal process" position. The pToC template is concrete, but the paper openly offers no method for weighing the evidence it catalogues. |
| [LIT-215](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-215.md) v2 | Defending Informational Structural Realism: The View of Alternatives | Karpenko (2025), DOI-10.5840/eps202562230. Karpenko argues against V.E. Terekhovich's non-eliminative OSR, which holds that entities and structures exist but "objects do not exist". He extends Floridi's informational structural realism with one thesis: empirically equivalent but structurally different models (wave/particle/field descriptions, superstring dualities, AdS/CFT holography, equivalent programs in digital physics) have equal ontological standing. Since nothing stands "behind" them with a privileged configuration, the descriptions, i.e. information, are themselves fundamental, and theoretical objects exist as ontological primitives. There is no formal argument, and the physics is presented by assertion, with several errors. | Rejected — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-096](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-096.md)); not worth a reader's time on this topic. It misreports its source (Floridi, [LIT-152](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-152.md)) on the points it builds on, and it states contested or wrong physics as established. Its one novel move, reading dualities as equal-status alternatives rather than underdetermination, is asserted, not argued, and is done properly in the duality literature ([LIT-113](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-113.md), [LIT-199](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-199.md)). |
| [LIT-217](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-217.md) v3 | Science, Metaphysics and Structural Realism | Ladyman (2001), DOI-10.21825/philosophica.82261. Ladyman argues that structural realism should be metaphysically, not epistemically, revisionary. He gives three grounds. Quantum statistics leaves the individuality of particles underdetermined: permutation invariance gives 3 two-particle states, not 4, so probabilities are 1/3 rather than 1/4 (p. 62). Entangled states give non-supervenient relations that refute Humean supervenience (pp. 71–73). The hole argument blocks point-based substantivalism (pp. 68–69). He proposes that science describes "the modal structure of the phenomena" (p. 73), with modal realism supplying the no-miracles intuition. The paper ends non-eliminatively: "the phenomena have structure but they are not structure" (p. 74). | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-192](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-192.md)); Worth reading as the earliest freely available statement of ontic structural realism by its originator. It argues the Humean-supervenience and quantum-individuality points more fully than the SEP survey ([LIT-045](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-045.md)). It also shows that the 2001 view was a modest one, realism about modal structure with no eliminativism, before *Every Thing Must Go*. Its positive proposal takes two paragraphs (pp. 73–74) and is programmatic. |
| [LIT-218](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-218.md) v2 | Ontic Structural Realism and Economics | Ross (2008), DOI-10.1086/594518. Ross argues that OSR, usually motivated only by fundamental physics, is also the right ontology for a mature special science, economics. The progress of economic theory from Jevons through Hicks–Allen (1934), Samuelson (1947), Debreu (1959) and Arrow (1965) consists in steadily removing psychological, individual-level hypotheses. Its basic objects are optimisation problems, above all games, which are "mathematical structures … whose relata are distinguished as such by the mathematical representations … just like quarks and bosons" (§3). So OSR, joined with an assumption that science is unified, gets consilient support from outside physics. Individuals, in physics and in economics, are "book-keeping devices". | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-189](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-189.md)); Worth reading as Ross's own short statement of what OSR says outside physics. It argues that individuals are bookkeeping heuristics while "tables and rocks" and people still exist, and that consilience across the sciences, not physics alone, can support OSR. Its history of economics is a sketch, and its central claims are asserted from the formalism rather than argued against a worked alternative. Cite the 2008 Philosophy of Science version. This note reads the 2006 preprint. |
| [LIT-219](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-219.md) v2 | Patterns All the Way Up: Prolegomena to a Future Naturalized Metaphysics | Ladyman (2026), DOI-10.7551/mitpress/15550.003.0006. Ladyman restates the Ladyman–Ross metaphysics as fifteen theses drawn from scientific practice. The existence criterion is "to be is to be a real pattern", a pattern that "indispensibly figures in projectible generalisations" (p. 2). Realism is realism about natural modal structure, which is "absolute" in formal mode but "domain and scale-dependent" in material mode (thesis 4). There is no single hierarchy of levels and no assumed fundamental level (theses 10–11, fn. 9). Ontology is effective and scale-relative (thesis 12). Scientific real patterns are lossy compressions, unlike the Game of Life's; the ideal gas laws use 3 degrees of freedom for ~10²³ (thesis 14). He quotes ETMG's Principle of Naturalistic Closure verbatim and calls it "problematic" because it refers to fundamental physics (p. 8). | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-191](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-191.md)); Worth reading as the most recent and most compact statement of rainforest realism by one of its two authors, and the one that explicitly revises *Every Thing Must Go*. It weakens the PNC, denies that "relational structure is fundamental" was meant as fundamentalism, and recasts real patterns modally and statistically as well as information-theoretically. Its fifteen theses are asserted and illustrated, not argued. It presupposes the book's definitions, which it does not restate. |
| [LIT-220](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-220.md) v2 | Real Patterns | Dennett (1991), DOI-10.2307/2027085. A pattern is real in some data "if there is a description of the data that is more efficient than the bit map, whether or not anyone can concoct it" (p. 34). This is Chaitin's incompressibility definition of randomness turned around (p. 32). Dennett uses the criterion, with the Game of Life's gliders and eaters as the stepping stone (pp. 37–42), to defend "mild realism" about beliefs. Folk psychology tracks a real, noisy pattern of enormous predictive leverage. Two rival interpretations can be "different, but equally real, patterns" with no deeper fact to settle between them (p. 49). | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-190](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-190.md)); Worth reading as the source of the real-patterns criterion that rainforest realism generalises into a theory of existence, and as the paper whose exact definition the later literature modifies. It has a lossless-compression criterion, observer-relativity through "perspectives", and trade-offs between noise and simplicity. Its target is beliefs, not ontology in general. Dennett explicitly declines the label question ("I think that the view itself is clearer than either of the labels", p. 51). |
| [LIT-222](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-222.md) v2 | No categorial support for radical ontic structural realism | Lam & Wüthrich (2015), DOI-10.1093/bjps/axt053. Lam and Wüthrich argue that category theory gives radical OSR no support. Identifying objects with identity arrows is relabelling (§3). Generalized elements X → A exist in every category, so elements are not eliminated (§4). Categories without products also lose set-style relations, "throwing out the relations with the relata" (§4). Morphisms relate C-objects, not the elements that stand for physical relata, and they "only distinguish isomorphism classes of structures" (§5). Bain's GR and TQFT cases eliminate at most spacetime points, not relata tout court (§§6–7). They conclude that category theory "offers little if any comfort to ROSR" (abstract) and favour "balanced" OSR. The Yoneda lemma is not named, although §§4–5 state two of its consequences. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-194](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-194.md)); Worth reading as the most careful direct refutation of Bain (yo2). Its main points (generalized elements, morphisms relate C-objects, determination only up to isomorphism, sections are not maximal ideals) are correct and are exactly what the Yoneda reading needs. It has a few category-theoretic slips of its own: Hilb said to lack products, a mis-definition of topos, and the claim that non-commutative algebras have no maximal ideals. |
| [LIT-223](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-223.md) v2 | Category-theoretic structure and radical ontic structural realism | Bain (2013), DOI-10.1007/s11229-011-9896-6. Bain argues that the "relations without relata" objection to radical OSR depends on defining structure set-theoretically, where a relation is a subset of X × X. If a structure is instead "an object in a category", its elements (arrows 1 → A) are "not essential", because category-theoretic objects need not be structured sets. His examples are sheaves of Einstein algebras for GR with asymptotic boundary conditions, which may lack global sections (§3), and nCob and Hilb (§4). He concludes that ROSR "avoids the charge that it rests on an incoherent claim" (p. 1634). The paper never mentions the Yoneda lemma, representable functors or universal properties by name. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-193](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-193.md)); Worth reading as the short, canonical statement of the category-theoretic defence of radical OSR, which the later literature (yo3; Lal & Teh; Eva 2016) responds to. Read it with yo3. Its central inference is overstated, and its GR section contains technical errors that yo3 documents. |

Whether scientific kinds are natural breaks into four questions (are the classifications natural, are they into kinds, what the kinds are, and do they have essences). | [LIT-276](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-276.md) v2 | Measurement as Sheafification: Context, Logic, and Truth after Quantum Mechanics | Ghose (2025), [ARXIV-2512.12249](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.12249). A programmatic essay, with no theorem, model or computation of its own. It restates Abramsky & Brandenburger's criterion (contextuality and non-locality as the absence of a global section of a presheaf over measurement contexts) and adds three things. It declares measurement to be "sheafification" of that presheaf, without specifying a site, a topology or any sheafified object. It asserts that the Ghose–Patra seven-valued logic is a finite Heyting algebra, without giving an order or operations. It proposes that a quantum potential scaled by 0 ≤ λ ≤ 1 (λ = 1 quantum, λ = 0 classical Hamilton–Jacobi) carries the presheaf continuously to a sheaf, which is asserted, not modelled. Its one worked formula, v2's Čech "obstruction class" [δs], is a coboundary and so is zero by construction. | Rejected — read in full 2026-09-27 ([NOTE-249](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-249.md)); not worth a reader's time for its formal claims. Every correct formal ingredient is Abramsky & Brandenburger's ([LIT-016](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-016.md)) or Abramsky, Mansfield & Barbosa's, and both are better read in the original. What the essay adds is either unconstructed (the sheafification, the site, the seven-element Heyting algebra, the link from λ to cohomology) or wrong as stated: v2's obstruction class is zero by construction, a sheaf topos is not in general Boolean, and classical distributions do not form a sheaf. Its only value is as a record of a position, the Bohrian reading of contextuality plus the Jaina analogy. |
